correctness.rationale: Square modulus reduces to a concave quadratic q(cos θ)=s²+b²+2bdx−(s²−d²)x². The nearest cosine samples u<0<v give two contacts. A quartic F(R) with F′>0 gives a unique R∈(0,1), and constructed positive coefficients balance those contacts. For every competitor the weighted convex two-sample lower functional has positive definite Hessian; selecting λ∈(0,1) makes the candidate its unique minimizer and certifies global face optimality for all odd N. Taylor expansion yields the stated N⁻² coefficient. Independently used direct nonsmooth sampled-grid optimization for N=5,7,9,11,21,101,501,1001 and found the analytic root ratio to numerical precision. This is not an extrapolation to all N.
